purpose: Close the cheap-baseline stage with interpretable nonlinear controls so a later TriQTO graph model cannot receive credit merely for generic magnitude or quadratic nonlinearity.

adaptive_development_disclosure.reason_for_followup: Step 6A showed weak signed-linear effect detection, a large exact-diagnostic mechanism gap, and reproducible graph-stat gains. This motivated pre-architecture magnitude and quadratic controls.

tasks.effect_detection: no_effect vs effect on all examples
tasks.integrated_diagnosis: effect prediction gates RZ/RX/RY into no_effect/RZ/RX/RY

magnitude_threshold_baselines.diag_rms_threshold: RMS of active finite-shot local, pairwise and parity B_delta coordinates
magnitude_threshold_baselines.diag_snr_proxy_threshold: diag RMS multiplied by sqrt(observed shots), a simple shot-noise-normalized effect score

diagonal_qda.covariance: class-specific diagonal variance shrunk toward unit variance after standardization
diagonal_qda.selection_metric: OOF balanced_accuracy then macro_f1 then larger shrinkage
diagonal_qda.binary_threshold_policy: select from training-root OOF score differences only

training_only_oof.fold_rule: reuse Step 6A four training-root folds from family_occurrence_index mod 5

required_questions: Does a direct diagnostic magnitude/SNR score recover effect presence better than signed linear diag_full?
Does diagonal quadratic nonlinearity materially improve finite-shot mechanism diagnosis?
Does simple graph context remain useful once a cheap nonlinear classifier is allowed?
How much exact-diagnostic headroom remains after the nonlinear control?
Is a dedicated graph architecture still scientifically justified rather than merely a generic nonlinear model?
